## v0.5.2-beta: clamd fix, original file names, easier troubleshooting

This release gets clamd running with the shipped configuration and keeps senders' file names by default. It also makes request-check failures easy to diagnose. It is the first release verified against a real ClamAV container in CI.

### Changed

- **Files keep their own names.** Files now arrive on the other side of the diode with the names they had on the sender's computer.
  - **Opt-in prefix:** a new checkbox, "Add the batch ID and my username to file names" (off by default), brings back the `<batch-id>_<seq>_<name>` form for a batch.
  - **Tracking:** the batch ID, username and original name are always recorded in the batch manifest and the audit log.
  - **Unsafe characters only:** names change only where a character cannot exist on Linux or Windows: directory parts, control characters, `< > : " / \ | ? *`, leading dots, leading and trailing spaces, trailing dots, and device names such as `CON`. Spaces, accents, other alphabets and other punctuation are kept. Names are capped at 180 bytes, keeping the extension.
  - **Visible renames:** the upload page shows "Arrives as: …" when a name had to change.
- **Same-name files never overwrite.** If a file with the same name, or its `.sha256`, is still in the outbox, the new file waits until the diode has collected both. With a 2-second settle time this normally takes under 15 seconds. The file is held for review if the old one is still there after an hour. Sidecars are also written without replacing anything.

### Fixed

- **clamd failed to start and stayed unhealthy.** The shipped `clamd.conf` set `LogFile /dev/stdout`, which clamd refuses inside a container ("Symbolic link loop"). The app correctly paused scanning, so nothing passed unscanned, but nothing was scanned either. The setting is removed. clamd also now listens on IPv6 as well as IPv4 inside the container.

### Added

- **Rejection logging.** When the upload page reports "request did not come from this site" or "reload the page and try again", the app logs a `request rejected` line. It shows the origin the browser sent next to the `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` it expected.
- **README Troubleshooting** rows for both messages.
- **CI job with the real `clamav/clamav:stable` image** and the shipped `clamd.conf`. It checks PING, VERSION, a clean file, EICAR detection, and that a file just over 4 GB is flagged as exceeding the limit rather than passed as OK.

### API

- `POST /api/v1/batches` accepts an optional `"prefix_names": true|false` (default `false`).
- `GET /api/v1/batches/{id}` returns `prefix_names`, and `sent_as` for each file whose outbox name differs from its own. Existing clients keep working.

### Upgrading from v0.5.1-beta

```sh
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose up -d --force-recreate clamd   # picks up the corrected clamd.conf
docker compose ps                             # clamd should become healthy
docker compose logs app | grep -i self-test   # wait for "clamd self-test passed"
```

If you customized `config/instructions.md`, keep your text and add the new point about file names.

**Tell the receiving side about the naming change.** File names now contain spaces and other punctuation, so receiving-side scripts must quote them. Two files with the same name can also arrive one after the other. How the receiving side handles that is open item 9 in the ICD.

### Still open

- No rate limiting in the app (nginx applies a coarse per-IP limit).
- No admin site. Quarantined and held files are handled on the host.
- No retention pruning yet for the audit log or quarantine.
